
### P4 


* P4 --- programming langauge for data planes
* intended to be compiled to run on fast switches
* includes ‘runtime’ defining how control plane configures data plane


### future P4 assignment  {.smaller}


* given:  

   * simple P4 switch that doesn't know where to direct frames
   * simpler controller (in Python) that configures switch
   * simulated 4-machine network in VM

* your task will be: 

   * have controller write static configuration to direct to right place
   * modify data plane to send information to control plane
   * have controller change configuration based on info from data plane

* (we'll discuss more details later)

### P4: switch parts  {.smaller}


```
V1Switch(
MyParser(),
MyVerifyChecksum(),
MyIngress(),
MyEgress(),
MyComputeChecksum(),
MyDeparser()
) main;

```
 

* code to declare instance of dataplane from functions for each part
* will look at most of these components 

   * won't have reason to change verify/compute checksum



### P4: declaring headers (1)  {.smaller}

    
<pre><code>typedef bit&lt;48&gt; macAddr_t;
<span data-fragment-index="0" class="fragment custom myem-only">@header</span> ethernet_t~ {
    macAddr_t srcAddr;
    macAddr_T dstAddr;
    bit&lt;16&gt;   etherType;
}
</code></pre>
 

* kinda like `typedef struct { ... } ethernet_t;`
* order needs to <i>exactly</i> match what's sent on network 

   * switch will do bit-by-bit copy into this struct



### P4: declaring headers (2)  {.smaller}

    
<pre><code><span data-fragment-index="0" class="fragment custom myem-only">struct headers</span> {
    <span data-fragment-index="1" class="fragment custom myem-only">ethernet_t</span>   ethernet;
    <span data-fragment-index="1" class="fragment custom myem-only">ipv4_t</span>       ipv4;
    <span data-fragment-index="1" class="fragment custom myem-only">ipv6_t</span>       ipv6;
}
</code></pre>
 

* struct of all possible headers 

   * from all layers the switch/router handles
   * not all frames will use all of them, some may be mutually exclusive
   * order does not need to match frame storage (will write code to handle that)

* references header types defined previously


### P4: parsing  {.smaller}


```
parser MyParser(
    packet_in packet,
    out headers hdr,
    inout metadata meta,
    inout standard_metadata_t standard_metadata) {

```
 

* function modifies ‘out’ parameters instead of returning
* parser function --- takes parameters: 

   * packet --- the input frame
   * headers --- extracted headers (<code>struct headers</code>)
   * meta --- program's local variables about frame (<code>struct metadata</code>)
   * standard_metadata --- info for system about frame 

      * where frame came from, where it should go, etc.




### P4: parsing  {.smaller}

    
<pre><code>parser MyParser(...) {
    <span data-fragment-index="0" class="fragment custom myem-only">state</span> start {
        <span data-fragment-index="1" class="fragment custom myem-only">transition</span> <span data-fragment-index="2" class="fragment custom myem-only">parse_ethernet</span>;
    }
    <span data-fragment-index="0" class="fragment custom myem-only">state</span> <span data-fragment-index="2" class="fragment custom myem-only">parse_ethernet</span> {
        <span data-fragment-index="3" class="fragment custom myem-only">packet.extract(hdr.ethernet);</span>
        <span data-fragment-index="1" class="fragment custom myem-only">transition</span> select(hdr.ethernet.etherType) {
            TYPE_IPV4: parse_ipv4;
            TYPE_IPV6: parse_ipv6
            default: accept;
        }
    }
    ....
}
</code></pre>

### P4: parsing  {.smaller}

    
<pre><code>parser MyParser(...) {
    ...
    state parse_ethernet {
        <span data-fragment-index="0" class="fragment custom myem-only">packet.extract(hdr.ethernet);</span>
        transition select(hdr.ethernet.etherType) {
            TYPE_IPV4: parse_ipv4;
            TYPE_IPV6: parse_ipv6
            default: accept;
        }
    }

    state parse_ipv4 {
        <span data-fragment-index="0" class="fragment custom myem-only">packet.extract(hdr.ipv4)</span>
        transition accept;
    }
    ....
}
</code></pre>
 ![](/switches/texfig/p4-dataplane-p4-parsing_2.figure-1.svg){.absolute top="0%" left="0%" width=1050 height=600 .my-center  .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=1}

### P4: deparsing  {.smaller}

    
<pre><code>control MyDeparser(packet_out packet, in headers hdr) {
    apply {
        <span data-fragment-index="0" class="fragment custom myem-only">packet.emit</span>(hdr.ethernet);
        <span data-fragment-index="0" class="fragment custom myem-only">packet.emit</span>(hdr.ipv4);
        <span data-fragment-index="0" class="fragment custom myem-only">packet.emit</span>(hdr.ipv6);
    }
}
</code></pre>
 ![](/switches/texfig/p4-dataplane-p4-deparsing.figure-1.svg){.absolute top="0%" left="0%" width=1050 height=600 .my-center  .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=1}

### switch decisions  {.smaller}


* most decisions switches/routers make are table lookups 
<hr class="vspace" />
* take field from packet (e.g. destination)
* lookup in table what to do with that (e.g. send to port X, throw error, etc.) 
<hr class="vspace" />
* P4 has special syntax for tables and table lookups


### P4: tables  {.smaller}

    
<pre><code><span data-fragment-index="0" class="fragment custom myem-only">table</span> mac_dst_exact {
    <span data-fragment-index="1" class="fragment custom myem-only">key</span> = {
        <span data-fragment-index="1" class="fragment custom myem-only">hdr.ethernet.dstAddr</span> : <span data-fragment-index="2" class="fragment custom myem-only">exact</span>;
    }
    <span data-fragment-index="1" class="fragment custom myem-only">actions</span> = {
        drop,
        forward_to,
    }
    size = 1024;
    default_action = drop();
}
</code></pre>
 ![](/switches/texfig/p4-dataplane-p4-tables.figure-1.svg){.absolute top="0%" left="0%" width=1050 height=600 .my-center  .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=1}
![](/switches/texfig/p4-dataplane-p4-tables.figure-2.svg){.absolute top="0%" left="0%" width=1050 height=600 .my-center  .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2}
![](/switches/texfig/p4-dataplane-p4-tables.figure-3.svg){.absolute top="0%" left="0%" width=1050 height=600 .my-center  .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3}
![](/switches/texfig/p4-dataplane-p4-tables.figure-4.svg){.absolute top="0%" left="0%" width=1050 height=600 .my-center  .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4}


### P4 table key types  {.smaller}


* exact --- full entry
* lpm --- longest prefix match 

   * table entries contain ‘prefixes’ of header field(s)
   * we'll see motivation for this when we talk about routing
   * if multiple entries match, take longest one

* ternary --- 0/1/don't care 

   * table entries contain key and mask
   * entry matches if bits included in mask match
   * other view: keys represented with 0/1/don't care ‘trits’



### content-addressable memory  {.smaller}


* high-end routers/switches have <i>content addressable memory</i> (CAM)
* … including <i>ternary content addressable memory</i> (TCAM) 
<hr class="vspace" />
* = hardware that implements a table lookup 

   * ‘content’ $\approx$ key being looked up
   * looks kinda like highly associative cache
   * probably lots of comparators

* allows multigigabit frame processing speeds
* P4 goal: P4 programs compile to use CAM/TCAM when available


### aside: TCAM cost  {.smaller}


* 2.7x more transistors than SRAM (common cache technology)
* probably much more power than SRAM
* hard to find recent quotes for price/power
* but probably 10s of dollars per megabyte 

   * e.g., secondary market price of Broadcom chip with 40Mbit of this is $\sim$\$180
   * chip needs 80W heatsink, max 900MHz clock rate
   * but chip has a bunch of other functionality, of course

### P4: actions  {.smaller}

    
<pre><code>control MyIngress(...) {
    <span data-fragment-index="0" class="fragment custom myem-only">action drop()</span> {
        mark_to_drop(<span data-fragment-index="1" class="fragment custom myem-only">standard_metadata</span>);
    }
    <span data-fragment-index="0" class="fragment custom myem-only">action forward_to(egressSpec_t port)</span> {
        <span data-fragment-index="1" class="fragment custom myem-only">standard_metadata.egress_spec = port;</span>
    }
    <span data-fragment-index="0" class="fragment custom myem-only">action mark_and_forward(egressSpec_t port)</span> {
        <span data-fragment-index="2" class="fragment custom myem-only">hdr.some_proto.value</span> = 1;
        <span data-fragment-index="1" class="fragment custom myem-only">standard_metadata.egress_spec = port;</span>
    }
    ...
}
</code></pre>
 ![](/switches/texfig/p4-dataplane-p4-actions.figure-1.svg){.absolute top="0%" left="0%" width=1050 height=600 .my-center  .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=1}

### P4: special actions  {.smaller}


* some ways switch can direct packet (incomplete list) 
<hr class="vspace" />
* send to the control plane 

   * special output port that goes to ‘general purpose’ CPU

* multicast/broadcast to multiple ports 

   * control plane can set <i>multicast groups</i>
   * makes multiple copies of packets
